VETERANS AFFAIRS COMMISSION MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, JUNE 4, 2025
  2525 GRAND AVENUE, LONG BEACH, 90815
  ROOM 204, 5:00 PM

Kenneth Osborn, Chair  James Goodin, Commissioner
Antawnette Atkins Blade, Vice Chair  Hershell Hardimon, Commissioner
Jerry Earl, Commissioner  Nicholas Sramek, Commissioner

  FINISHED AGENDA & MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Osborn called the meeting to order at 5:08 p.m.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present: Goodin, Osborn, Sramek, Atkins Blade

Also present: Gina Overholt, Coordinator.

Also in attendance: Christina Boatwright, Hershell Hardimon, Linda Rick, Rosie Rubin and Steve
Hageman.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Pledge of Allegiance
 The Commission and everyone present recited the Pledge of Allegiance.
 Chair Report
 The banners subcommittee may determine where selected banners may be installed based on
whether there is a connection between the individual and the banner location. For example, if a
finalist selected for the program wrote in their bio about their connection to the VA Long Beach, then
that banner may be installed on Bellflower near the VA Hospital. It is likely that only 20 or so of the
banners may be linked to any of the three banner locations. As such, two-thirds of the banner
locations will be randomized.
 Staff Report
 Staff liaison Overholt shared that up to two new Commissioners will be sworn in at the Council
meeting on June 10, reminded the Commissioners that there is no Commission meeting on July 9,
and thanked the Commissioner who volunteered at the event, Commissioners Osborn, Blade, Goodin
and former Commissioner Schotter.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  25-55491  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Veterans Affairs Commission
  meeting of Wednesday, May 14, 2025.

2.  25-55492  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on the Veterans Banner
  Program.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Atkins Blade, seconded by
  Commissioner Sramek, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by
  the following vote:

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 0  None

  Rosie Rubin, daughter of Tibor Rubin, who was honored in last year’s banner
  program, addressed the Commission to express her deep gratitude to the city and
  the Commission for the Veterans banners program. Rubin was a Holocaust survivor
  who immigrated to the U.S., who joined the Army and was presented the Medal of
  Honor for military valor during the Korean War. In 2005, he received the
  Congressional Medal of Honor. The VA Long Beach Healthcare System is named
  for Rubin. The 25 banners installed in 2024 were recently removed and distributed
  to each of the Veterans or their families. Ms. Rubin accepted her father’s banner on
  behalf of her family. She displayed Rubin’s banner while standing with members of
  the Commissioners and the staff liaison for photos.

  Updates on the 2025 banners program followed. Project in final design phase. A
  few design options are being considered for the USS Frank E. Evans banner
  because it recognizes the Lost 74 who perished in 1969 and not an individual
  Veteran. The finalists and their families will be notified of their selection in the
  coming days. Banners are scheduled for installation on July 7, pending city
  approval of the permit and review and sign off by the Veterans or their families.
  Veterans and their families will be invited to a meet and greet, which will be part of
  a scheduled health screening event coordinated by a local non-profit organization
  on August 30. This is in place of a media event, an option discussed in previous
  Commission meetings. Commissioners Blade and Goodin offered to work with the
  non-profit to plan and promote this event.

3.  25-55493  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on the commemoration of the
  USS Frank E. Evans and Lost 74, which occurred on June 3, 2025.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Sramek, seconded by Commissioner
  Goodin, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 0  None

  Remembering the USS Frank E. Evans Lost 74, was a successful, well-done, well-
  attended that aptly demonstrates the power of partnership between the city and the
  Veteran-led local organizations that take on a variety of important causes. This is a
  model for future city partnerships with Veteran-led, Veteran-serving organizations.

4.  25-55494  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation on a proposed housing project
  for Veterans at 1400 Cherry.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Atkins Blade, seconded by Doplemore,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 0  None

  Developer Steve Hageman shared additional details about this 100-unit
  development to provide housing and support services for Veterans. Project is in the
  pre-planning approval phase. Discussion followed with the Commission taking a
  lead on connecting the developer with Council District 6, where the project is
  located. Vice Chair Blade will reach out to Councilmember Saro to schedule a
  conversation about the project. Chair Osborn will reach out to the mayor’s office
  and additional contacts in relevant city departments.

PUBLIC COMMENT

No public comment.
